passage:
"Ammi, guess what! Ma'am changed the seats and now I sit with Sudha."
"The girl with the two plaits?"
"Yes! And guess what she had in her pencil box? Cricket cards! The shiny ones!"
"Oh ho. So that's why you're smiling like that."
"She has two fast bowlers and I have three wicketkeepers. I gave her one keeper and she gave me a bowler. Fair trade."
"Did you talk about anything else?"
"Umm... she hates bhindi too. And she knows the joke about the elephant in the fridge."
"Is she your friend now?"
"I think so. Tomorrow she's bringing her doubles. Can I take my whole box?"
"Only if you don't lose it on the bus, Tanvir. My son loses everything."
"I won't! Sudha said we can keep them in the middle of the bench, half-half."

qa.q: What cards did Sudha and Tanvir each have?
qa.a: Sudha has two fast bowlers and Tanvir has three wicketkeepers.

qa.q: What does Tanvir's 'guess what' suggest about how he feels?
qa.a: He is excited and happy about his new friend: he keeps saying 'guess what', chatters about the shiny cards and wants to take his whole box tomorrow. 😊

qa.q: How could Ammi help this new friendship grow?
qa.a: Ammi could let Tanvir take some cards, ask about Sudha with interest, and remind him to keep them safe, without making it a big deal.

qa.q: How might Sudha see the trade?
qa.a: Sudha probably enjoys having someone right beside her who likes the same cards, and the fair swap shows her that Tanvir shares fairly.

grounding: Shows two bench partners discovering a shared love of cricket cards and starting a friendship through trading and small jokes.

passage:
My name is Indu and I'm nine. At the start of term, Miss put me next to Payal on the second bench, by the window. I didn't know her at all. She was quiet and I was quiet.
On the third day, I saw the corner of a cricket card sticking out of her geometry box. I have forty-two of those at home! I whispered, "Do you have a spinner?" She went pink and pulled out six.
After that we traded every lunch break. We made a rule: no swapping a card you only have one of. Then we started a joke that the pigeon on the window ledge was our umpire.
I still don't know her birthday or her favourite colour. But I know she saves her chapati for last, and I know she gives fair trades.

qa.a: Miss put Indu next to Payal on the second bench, by the window.

qa.q: What was Indu thinking when the card showed in Payal's geometry box?
qa.a: Indu was excited and saw a chance to talk, because Indu has forty-two of those cards at home.

qa.q: What small step helped Indu and Payal start talking?
qa.a: Indu whispered one simple question about a spinner card; a shared interest gave two quiet children something easy to talk about. 🙂

qa.q: What might it have been like for Payal when Indu whispered to her?
qa.a: Payal may have felt shy but pleased; she went pink and then pulled out six cards, so she was ready to share.

grounding: Illustrates a friendship that starts from sitting on the same bench and sharing cricket cards and a joke, before the children know much about each other.
